questions.heading: One Schema Validates the Whole Snapshot and Reports Every Problem in One Pass
questions.stem: A snapshot arrives with a negative cost on one project and a parent id that names no project. The schema bounds each field and checks references in a model validator on the whole snapshot (mode="after"). What does the first validation report?

options.text: Both problems, since pydantic collects every error before it raises
options.says: Field errors are collected together, but the snapshot's after-validator runs only once every field is valid, so the reference problem is not reported yet.

options.text: Only the cost, since the reference rule runs once every field is valid
options.says: Right: field problems come first; the reference rule runs on a snapshot whose fields all passed.

options.text: Only the parent, since rules across records run before any field rule
options.says: The order is the other way round: an after-validator sees the validated fields, so it runs after them.

options.text: Neither problem, since validation stops at the first record that fails
options.says: Pydantic does not stop at the first bad field; the lesson's run reported four field problems in one pass.

questions.heading: At a Machine Boundary, Forbid Unknown Keys and Turn Off Guessing
questions.stem: An exporter renames the key parent_lag to lag in every project. The schema declares parent_lag: NonNegativeInt = 0 and leaves pydantic's extra setting at its default. What happens to the document?

options.text: It is refused, since a field the schema needs is missing everywhere
options.says: parent_lag has a default, so its absence is not an error; the default fills it.

options.text: It is refused, since every key it sends must match a declared field
options.says: That is extra="forbid". The default is "ignore", which drops unknown keys.

options.text: It is accepted, and lag is kept as an extra field on each project
options.says: Keeping unknown keys is extra="allow"; the default drops them.

options.text: It is accepted, and every project's lag silently becomes zero
options.says: Right: lag is ignored, parent_lag is missing, and its default 0 fills the gap with no error.

questions.heading: The Schema Is a Versioned Contract, Published as JSON Schema
questions.stem: An older depot system still sends documents in which one column has its old name. The service's schema is strict, forbids unknown keys and requires schema_version 3. What should the service do with those documents?

options.text: Upgrade each with an explicit rename step, then validate it as version 3
options.says: Right: an upgrade step that knows what the old name meant brings the document forward, and the schema stays strict.

options.text: Validate each with extra="ignore", so the old column drops and the rest is used
options.says: Dropping the old column lets a default stand in for its value: the quiet failure the lesson showed with lag.

options.text: Validate each with strict=False, so the old column converts to the new one
options.says: Strict mode is about value types, not key names; lax mode renames nothing.

options.text: Accept any version number, so documents from every exporter can pass
options.says: Then an old document is read as if it were new, which is what the version field exists to stop.
